research_notes: The eventual runtime contract can define a minimum useful-unit granularity so late-turn work remains checkpointable.
Too-large units reduce ability to stop near hard cap; too-small units can create excessive control/I/O overhead.
Policy comparison should therefore use realistic unit-size distributions rather than only microtasks.
The current mixed profile is checkpoint-heavy and bounded, suitable for safety exploration but not sufficient alone for final generalization.
Cross-profile replication remains required near the candidate boundary.
No current evidence changes that requirement.
